title.narrative: Ugandan farmers bring back their livestock through Circular Maggot farming, Kabanyolo, Uganda

description.narrative: Ugandan coffee farmers usually also keep livestock to maintain stable incomes and need a cheap and non-fluctuating price and quality to feed their livestock, one that does not negatively impact the environment as the current Silverfish does. In Uganda, the over fishing of silverfish is posing a serious harm to its population and its surrounding ecosystem and creates issues with neighbouring countries Kenya and Tanzania. Silverfish is currently used to add a fatty protein source to animal feed but prices are increasing and supply decreasing which is causing farmers to stop their business. Maggots offer a reliable, sustainable, environmental-friendly and waste-to-protein alternative and can also be used as a fertiliser.Furthermore, maggots are cultivated using organic waste, which offers a solution to help farmers and other companies get rid of their waste and thus enabling a circular model. Marula Agribusiness wants to set up the first commercial maggot farm in Uganda by working together with local coffee and livestock farmers and local food companies to supply their organic waste to cultivate maggots and transfer these in fertilisers and protein to feed livestock of farmers. In order to prepare for further investments, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provides financial support to this pilot project with the aim to test the entire supply chain and market. The project includes the set-up of an operational factory and warehouse in Kabanyolo with production capacity up to 5,000 kg per week, establishing a partnership with local university Makerere Research Institute Kabanyolo (MAURIK), training local farmers and local waste suppliers, conducting a study into maggots as a valuable protein source for a variety of animals, as well as the development of a scalable business plan for future investments. The project currently supports 10 direct jobs, 45 indirect jobs and has already provided training to 670 farmers on circular farming using maggots. The full-scale maggot farm has been set-up and also functions as a research centre. Upon successful completion of the pilot, further upscaling will take place. The model has the potential to be replicated in mini-farms across the country which, due its circular and small scale nature, will have a massive (positive) disruptive impact on the current silver fishing industry, livestock farming, the livelihoods of farmers and the environment.
